topicName: Animal tissues, organs and organ systems

cards.front: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
cards.back: It pumps blood around the whole body at higher pressure, so it needs more muscle. The right ventricle only pumps blood to the nearby lungs.
cards.hint: Think about how far each side of the heart pumps blood.

cards.front: How are alveoli adapted for rapid gas exchange?
cards.back: Their large number gives a **large surface area**. Their walls are one cell thick, so gases diffuse over a short distance.

cards.front: Why are capillary walls only one cell thick?
cards.back: This gives substances a **short diffusion distance** between the blood and the body's tissues.
cards.hint: Think about how distance affects the speed of diffusion.

cards.back: An **organ system** is a group of organs working together to carry out a major function.

cards.front: What is the order of blood flow from the body, through the heart and lungs, and back to the body?
cards.back: Vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta, body.
cards.hint: Start where blood enters the heart from the body.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to say that arteries always carry oxygenated blood?
cards.back: The **pulmonary artery** carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, whatever its oxygen level.
cards.hint: Check which vessel travels to the lungs.

cards.back: **Veins** are blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart at lower pressure. They have valves to prevent backflow.
cards.hint: Compare their direction and pressure with arteries.

cards.front: Why are red blood cells biconcave in shape?
cards.back: Their biconcave shape gives them a **large surface area** for exchange of gases.

cards.front: What do platelets do in the blood?
cards.back: They help blood **clot**, reducing blood loss and limiting the entry of pathogens.
cards.hint: Think about what happens when the body is cut.

cards.back: **Ventilation** is the movement of air into and out of the lungs, which replaces the air in the alveoli.

cards.front: How does oxygen move from an alveolus into the blood?
cards.back: Oxygen dissolves in the moist lining of the alveolus, then **diffuses** from the air in the alveolus into the blood.
cards.hint: Think about what must happen before a gas can diffuse.

cards.back: **Coronary arteries** are blood vessels that supply the heart muscle with oxygenated blood.
cards.hint: Think about which organ these arteries serve.

cards.front: How does a diet high in saturated fat affect the heart?
cards.back: It raises **blood cholesterol**, which increases the risk of fatty deposits narrowing the coronary arteries.

cards.front: Why is it wrong to say that smoking certainly causes heart disease?
cards.back: Lifestyle factors **increase or decrease risk**; they do not guarantee that someone will develop disease. Inherited factors cannot be changed.
